metadata.case_name: LAW PING LEUNG v. NG SZE PONG

injuries.description: Contusion over the right temporal region with traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage
source: Computed tomography showed contusion over the right temporal region with traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage.

injuries.icd_description: Fracture of base of skull, unspecified

injuries.description: Area of 8 cm x 12 cm depression on his skull (cosmetic/depressive defect)
source: Cosmetically, there is an area of 8 cm x 12 cm depression on his skull and he was described by Dr C.K. Lam as having a “weird” and “angry” appearance.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of vault of skull, unspecified

source: He had fractured right clavicle together with bilateral lung contusion with pneumothorax.
He had fractured right clavicle together with bilateral lung contusion with pneumothorax.

injuries.description: Multiple lacerations over the limbs, his left eye and left knee
source: He had multiple lacerations over the limbs, his left eye and left knee.
He also has mild dysphagia (difficulty of swallowing) and mild left hemiparesis (weakness of one side of his body).

injuries.description: Post-traumatic seizures (three episodes of grand mal seizures)
source: He has suffered three episodes of grand mal seizures with loss of consciousness, generalized convulsive movements and uprolling of the eyeballs.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

manifestations.description: Unconscious on admission with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 7/15
Poor cognition and memory; thinking process and memory substantially impaired; slow and sometimes irrelevant responses; difficulty learning and retaining new information; recent memory poor
Needs to be reminded of appointments; often forgets what he has done a moment ago or where he has placed his belongings
Has to be accompanied when going outdoors because his sense of direction is poor
Intermittent headaches of a dragging character, mild intensity, occur once or twice a week, each attack about 2 minutes
Intermittent dizziness of mild intensity, occurs once a week, brief, brought on by riding on buses
Personality change: became easily irritable and no longer sociable
Weakness of limbs, especially left leg; cannot squat down; needs to hold on to furniture for support when putting on his trousers
Three episodes of grand mal seizures with loss of consciousness and generalized convulsive movements

treatments_received: Emergency burr hole operation for intracranial pressure monitoring and clot evacuation
Intensive care unit care (including mechanically assisted ventilation) for 2 weeks
Tracheostomy (performed on 12 September 2006) with tracheostomy weaned off on 16 October 2006
Shoulder immobilizer for right clavicle fracture
Transfer to Shatin Hospital for rehabilitation

losses.description: Area of 8 cm x 12 cm depression on skull causing a 'weird' and 'angry' appearance
Became easily irritable and no longer sociable

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Has to be accompanied when going outdoors because his sense of direction is poor

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Needs to hold on to furniture for support when putting on his trousers; cannot squat down

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: The parties no longer had sex after the accident (wife's evidence)
No longer sociable; wife's social life greatly affected; family life altered
